newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil futures end firmer but off highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil futures end firmer but off highs.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended firmer but were pulled back from early highs by profit taking into the close, traders said.
The May gas oil contract last traded $2.75 up at $163.25 a tonne after touching a high of $164.75 boosted in early trade by stronger crude and as cold U.S. weather boosted sentiment.
The May/June spread stood $1.75 in contango.

Traders said the market initially firmed on news that a new cold spell would affect the United States up to early next week and as news of a row between Germany and Iran over the killing of Kurdish exiles pushed crude futures higher.
Physical gas oil tracked the futures gains with barge and cargo premiums to the May contract holding steady despite slack buying.
Diesel prices continued to be supported by tightish supplies although actual buying interest here too was quiet.
May Brent futures were holding steady around 18 cents up at $18.11 a barrel stuck in the middle of a narrow 16 cent trading range.
